metadata.scope: exact Hecke/Euler-product identification plus finite summatory diagnostic; no directional shell asymptotic theorem

exact_identification.angular_character: xi_k(a)=exp(i*k*arg(a)) on odd Gaussian ideals; use k=8*l
exact_identification.l0: H_0=G; the series has a double pole at s=1 with leading coefficient 1/pi
exact_identification.l_ge_1: xi_{8l} is nontrivial; the series has a simple pole at s=1 with residue rho_l=8*L(1,xi_{8l})/pi^2
exact_identification.selberg_delange_consequence: Using the same published Selberg-Delange level admitted in Stage12: sum_{n<=X}G(n)~X log X/pi and sum_{n<=X}H_l(n)~rho_l X for fixed l>=1.

normalization_recovery.meaning: the nonmultiplicative G-neutral denominator becomes a uniformly convergent sum of fixed-j multiplicative local channels after the prime-local numerator is split into U_F-delta_{g=1}.

outer_scale_parameterization.primitive_base: u>v, gcd(u,v)=1, u-v odd, scale k=gcd(p,z)
outer_scale_parameterization.surviving_scale_support: k is odd; any q=3 mod 4 dividing k kills the primitive transformed numerator, so effective k is supported on q=1 mod 4

validation.note: mean_H1 is numerically stable near 0.60844 through 5e6; this is a finite diagnostic, not a proof of the residue value.

references: Rudnick-Waxman, Angles of Gaussian primes, arXiv:1705.07498 (Gaussian ideal direction e^{4 i theta}; Hecke angular framework).
On Gaussian primes in sparse sets, Compositio Mathematica, section 2.7 (xi_k(z)=(z/|z|)^k and Hecke L(s,xi_k chi) on Q(i)).
